overview: A timing belt has evenly-spaced teeth molded into it that mesh with matching teeth on a pulley, transmitting rotational motion without slipping the way a plain flat belt or friction drive would — critical in CNC machines and 3D printers, where a single skipped tooth means a positioning error baked permanently into whatever's being made. This pairing is how a stepper motor's rotation becomes precise linear motion along an axis: the motor turns a pulley, the belt is clamped to a moving carriage, and the carriage travels a distance calculated exactly from the belt's tooth pitch and the pulley's tooth count.
simpleSummary: A toothed belt and pulley set that transmits motion precisely without slipping, as used in 3D printers.

specifications.commonProfile: GT2 (2mm tooth pitch) is the standard in 3D printers/hobby CNC
specifications.pulleyToothCount: Commonly 16-20 teeth for small motor pulleys
specifications.material: Rubber/polyurethane belt with fiberglass or steel tension cords; aluminum or plastic pulleys

pinMap.name: Belt Teeth
pinMap.function: The molded teeth that mesh with the pulley, providing slip-free motion transfer.
pinMap.gotcha: Belt tension matters as much as tooth engagement — too loose causes skipped teeth/backlash, too tight adds friction and wears the belt and bearings faster.

pinMap.name: Pulley Bore
pinMap.function: Center hole mounting the pulley to a motor shaft, usually with a set screw.

pinMap.name: Idler Pulley Mount
pinMap.function: A free-spinning pulley (often just a bearing) at the opposite end of the belt path, providing tension and a return path.

useCases.title: 3D printer / CNC axis motion
useCases.scenario: Convert a stepper motor's rotation into precise linear carriage motion along X/Y axes.

useCases.title: Robotic arm joint drive
useCases.scenario: Transmit motor torque to a joint located some distance away from the motor itself.

oftenConfusedWith: Plain friction belts (can slip, no positional precision)
oftenUpgradedTo: Ball screws for even higher precision and rigidity in CNC applications
